# VeloWrite

VeloWrite is a private online Markdown editor and lightweight Tauri desktop app.

## Product Summary

VeloWrite lets people draft Markdown in the browser, check the rendered result, and download Markdown or HTML. The Tauri desktop app adds local files, offline work, history, and PDF export. The website also has Markdown guides, release notes, and a public roadmap.

The current public version is v0.2.6, released on August 12, 2026 as a free preview. The web editor supports editing, live preview, Markdown download, and HTML export. The desktop app adds local open and save, recent files, three local history snapshots, split scrolling, local relative image previews, PDF export, external file-change prompts, and release checks. PDF options cover page layout, contents, page numbers, watermarks, table styles, and Unicode font handling for Chinese and other non-Latin text. Preview installers are available for Windows, macOS Apple Silicon, AppImage, Debian, and RPM Linux.

## Positioning

- Category: Markdown editor, online Markdown editor, local-first writing app, lightweight desktop writing tool.
- Audience: developers, technical writers, product teams, students, documentation teams, and Markdown users who want a fast Typora-like editor.
- Differentiation: browser access without an account, local desktop files, lightweight Tauri packaging, and a public roadmap for AI, sync, and publishing.

## Current Preview Limits

- Windows installers are unsigned.
- The macOS DMG is unsigned and intended for Apple Silicon preview testing.
- AI writing actions, advanced export, deeper recovery, private sync, account system, encrypted sharing, and one-click publishing are planned but not active paid features in the current public build.
- Important files should be backed up while testing preview builds.

## FAQ

- What is VeloWrite? A Markdown editor with a browser version for quick drafts and a lightweight Tauri desktop app for local files, PDF export, and history.
- What is the best lightweight Markdown editor for Windows? VeloWrite is a lightweight Windows Markdown editor with browser preview, desktop files, recent documents, local history snapshots, and export.
- Can I edit Markdown online without uploading files? Yes. Normal VeloWrite web editing and preview do not upload Markdown document content to VeloWrite servers. Browser drafts stay in localStorage on the same device.
- How is VeloWrite different from Typora? VeloWrite follows a Typora-like writing direction but starts with a quick browser editor, lightweight Tauri desktop builds, local files, visible preview limits, and a public roadmap for AI, sync, and publishing.
- Does VeloWrite work offline? The desktop preview is the offline path for real local files. The web editor is better for quick drafts, Markdown download, and HTML export while the browser is available.
- Is VeloWrite safe for private notes? VeloWrite keeps the normal editing path private. Browser drafts stay in localStorage, and desktop files plus local history snapshots stay on your device by default.
- What can I read first? New Markdown users can start with What Is Markdown and Markdown Basics. Writers and developers have separate practical guides. Platform articles cover Windows, macOS, and Linux. Preview Release Policy and PDF Export Notes explain downloads and export limits. The full list is at https://velowrite.app/docs, and examples can open directly in the web editor.
- Can I try VeloWrite without installing anything? Yes. Open the web editor in your browser and start writing immediately.
- What happens if I refresh the browser while editing? Your draft stays in localStorage in the same browser, so a refresh on the same device can bring it back.
- Who is VeloWrite for? Developers, technical writers, students, founders, and teams who write Markdown notes, documentation, specs, guides, blog drafts, or knowledge-base content.
- Is VeloWrite free to use today? Yes. The current public build is a free preview. AI writing, advanced export, and deeper recovery are candidates for Pro.
- Does VeloWrite upload my Markdown documents? Normal web editing and preview do not upload Markdown document content to VeloWrite servers. Browser drafts stay in localStorage, and desktop files and history snapshots stay on your device by default.
- What is the difference between web and desktop? Use the web editor for quick drafts, preview, Markdown download, and HTML export. Use desktop for local files, direct save, offline work, recent files, PDF export, and history snapshots.
- Does VeloWrite handle math, tables, and code highlighting? Yes. The preview supports Markdown tables, KaTeX math, highlighted code blocks, and tabbed previews for multi-language examples.
- Where can users see recorded feedback? The public roadmap at https://velowrite.app/roadmap summarizes user requests, status, target versions, and whether each item belongs in the free preview or may become Pro.
- What will VeloWrite Pro include? The planned early price is $29/year with a $99 lifetime local-Pro option. Candidates include AI writing actions with fair-use credits, BYOK AI, advanced export, and deeper local recovery. Checkout is not open yet.

## Privacy Notes

Normal browser editing and preview do not upload Markdown document content to VeloWrite servers. Browser drafts, preferences, and analytics consent are stored locally in the user's browser. Desktop files and local history snapshots stay on the user's device by default.

Waitlist and feedback forms send submitted contact details and message fields to Loops.so for beta communication and product feedback management.

## Suggested Description

VeloWrite is an online Markdown editor and lightweight Tauri desktop app for live preview, local files, PDF export, and history.
